problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}=3xy,\,y(1)=2
$$

Use Euler's method with one step to approximate $y(2).$
worked_solution:
Since we want to find the value of $y$ at $x=2,$ we will use a step size of 

$$
Δx=2-1=1.
$$

First, we add the initial condition data:

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $\,Δy\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $1$ | $2$ |  |  |

Next, we compute ${y}^{′}$ according to the given rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =3xy \\  & =3\cdot 1\cdot 2 \\  & =6\end{aligned}
$$

So, we add this to our table:

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $\,Δy\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $1$ | $2$ | $6$ |  |

Next, we compute $Δy$ using Euler's method:

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & ={y}^{′}\cdot Δx \\  & =(6)\cdot 1 \\  & =6\end{aligned}
$$

We add this to our table:

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $\,Δy\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $1$ | $2$ | $6$ | $6$ |

To get the values of $x$ and $y$ in the *next* row, we add $Δx$ to $x$ and $Δy$ to $y,$ as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{\text{new}} & =x+Δx \\  & =1+1 \\  & =2 \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy \\  & =2+6 \\  & =8\end{aligned}
$$

Adding these results to our table gives the following:

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $\,Δy\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $1$ | $2$ | $6$ | $6$ |
| $2$ | $8$ |  |  |

Therefore, we conclude that $y(2)≈8.$
